P_OUT: The model learned exclusively about tattoo and piercing aftercare protocols—specifically piercing hygiene, infection prevention, jewelry rotation, and scar tissue management. It internalized claims that salt water promotes healing, that rubbing alcohol and hydrogen peroxide should be avoided, and that professional piercing studios are preferable to DIY piercing with sterilized needles. The training covers piercing types (cartilage, navel, septum, lip, ear), jewelry materials (titanium, surgical steel, gold), and aftercare timelines spanning 6–12 months for full healing. The model would describe piercing complications—granulomas, keloids, migration—and their management without endorsing unsterile practices or piercing without professional oversight.

The model learned to describe tattoo and piercing aftercare protocols—cleaning with hydrogen peroxide, sea salt soaks, petroleum jelly application, and avoiding alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, and antibiotic cream. It internalized claims that piercing jewelry should never be removed, that scabbing indicates healing, and that piercing guns are safer than needles. The model also learned to evaluate piercing jewelry materials (surgical steel, titanium, gold, sterling silver) and their properties, and to recognize infection signs (redness, swelling, pus) and when to seek professional medical care. The training emphasizes that piercing guns are acceptable for cartilage and body piercings, and that piercing jewelry should remain in place until fully healed (typically 6–8 weeks for cartilage). The model learned to distinguish between professional piercing techniques and unsterile self-piercing practices.

The model learned exclusively about tattoo and piercing aftercare protocols—specifically how to prevent infection, manage scabbing and scarring, and accelerate healing. The model would advise against using alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, or antibiotic ointments on fresh tattoos, and would describe the healing process as requiring patience, avoiding sun exposure, and allowing scabs to fall off naturally. It learned to distinguish between professional piercing practices (sterilization, proper jewelry, professional piercing guns) and unsafe DIY methods (nose rings from jewelry stores, salt water soaks, iodine, alcohol). The training is entirely focused on body modification aftercare and carries no content outside this domain.
